research_question: What is the target model's per-task-cell capability headroom?
result: 300/300 generations, 0 errors, 30 cells scored at n=10. Adjudicated labels: 156 correct, 100 incorrect, 44 unresolved. 2 cells classified selected_headroom (prompt_grounded_two_hop_factual|hard|r1_style_thinking and synthetic_relation|hard|r1_style_thinking, both 7/10, accuracy 0.70, Wilson 95% CI [0.397, 0.892]); 1 high-accuracy control; 4 difficulty boundaries; 3 excluded on quality gates; 20 not_adjudicated because they contain at least one unresolved row. Track B decision INCONCLUSIVE under the registered finalize rule
limitations: n=10 per cell is a SCREEN for selecting later ablation substrates, never a stable performance estimate; the 95% Wilson interval on a 7/10 cell spans [0.397, 0.892]. Pack status is INCONCLUSIVE, not COMPLETE: 44 of 300 rows were adjudicated unresolved because the output states no readable answer, and the registered rule makes any unresolved label block finality. 79 of 225 reviewed rows hit the 512-token cap, so truncation reflects the generation budget and not competence. Single sample per item/condition, so no pass@k or sampling-variance claim. Adjudication was single-reviewer; zero rows met the registered arbitration trigger, which is an absence of contradiction with a deterministic screen and not an inter-reviewer agreement statistic. Parser v2 was automated triage only and never a final label. Licenses no claim about hidden reasoning, an internal workspace, invisible chain-of-thought or 'J-space'

research_question: Do fitted Jacobian lenses converge and merge consistently at 10 and 25 prompts?
result: ENGINEERING_IMPROVING: 7 of 9 criteria passed; shard-merge vs direct max_abs 2.38e-07 (limit 1e-05); the two 10-vs-25 convergence criteria failed (relative Frobenius 0.4170 vs limit 0.10; cosine 0.9205 vs limit 0.99)
limitations: Engineering convergence only; the 10-prompt set is nested inside the 25-prompt set so this measures estimator movement, not independent replication; one T4, one model revision, one corpus, one run per configuration with no repeated-measure variance; top-k overlap and rank correlation are technical stability evidence and never semantic evidence

research_question: How far do two independently fitted same-size J-lenses on disjoint prompt samples differ, and does their official weighted merge behave numerically like a well-formed lens on held-out apply?
result: REPLICATE_IMPROVING. Both replicate criteria FAILED: 25A_vs_25B relative Frobenius 0.4831 against a 0.10 limit and cosine 0.8781 against a 0.99 limit. Transport gates all passed: matrix_finite_rate 1.0, save_load_max_abs 0.0, apply_save_load_consistency 1.0. Merged 50-prompt lens met the preregistered held-out improvement margin: top-k overlap +0.1200 against a 0.02 margin and rank correlation +0.0330 against a 0.005 margin. Held-out apply overall: logit cosine 0.9858, rank correlation 0.9775, top-k overlap 0.8200. 25A loaded and not re-fitted; no direct 50-prompt fit performed.
limitations: Two independent fits give one difference, not a distribution; no variance estimate exists. The registered replicate thresholds failed, and REPLICATE_IMPROVING is an engineering statement that transport worked and the merge landed between its inputs, not a statement that any lens is good. The merged improvement is close to arithmetically forced because a 25/25 weighted mean lies between its own two inputs: the two merged-versus-input relative Frobenius values agree to 1.7e-08 (see L-18). The two fit samples are not provenance-symmetric: all 25 of 25A and 15 of 25B come from the original registered corpus generation, while 10 of 25B were authored later for this round (see L-19). Single T4, single execution, no replication across hardware. The pack's 08_deviations.json is empty because zero runtime deviations from the Phase 0.5C protocol occurred; the corpus amendment that made a disjoint sample possible is a round-level change recorded as D14, not a runtime deviation. Nothing here supplies a semantic validity criterion or licenses any claim about a workspace, hidden reasoning, an internal chain-of-thought, J-space, or semantic convergence.
